[Javaagent] This selector only controls the suspend-function module. `KotlinCoroutinesFlowInstrumentationModule` remains default-enabled under `kotlinx-coroutines` and registers the Flow async-end strategy used by the default-enabled generic `@WithSpan` instrumentation, so methods returning `Flow` still receive full `@WithSpan` instrumentation by default. This contradicts the new documented default and the claim that the broad selector no longer enables annotations. Move the Flow registration under the same default-off selector (and cover the Flow operation in the disabled JVM).

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: Generic @WithSpan instrumentation (opentelemetry-instrumentation-annotations-1.16) is a separate default-enabled module and already instruments Flow-returning methods regardless of the coroutines selector; the Flow module only registers an async end strategy so the span ends on flow completion. Gating it default-off would make Flow spans end at method return, a regression. The PR's selector only governs the suspend-function annotation module, which is what the changelog/README state.

Upsides: Keeps correct Flow span end timing.

Downsides: Flow-returning @WithSpan methods remain traced by default via the generic module.

Users who run with global instrumentation disabled and explicitly enable `kafka-clients-metrics-0.11`, `kafka-clients-0.11`, `kotlinx-coroutines-1.0`, `kotlinx-coroutines-opentelemetry-instrumentation-annotations`, or `opentelemetry-instrumentation-annotations` are also affected, but the migration note currently does not identify those configurations. List every removed alias so those users can migrate to the dedicated selectors.

threads.body: [General] The `kotlinx-coroutines-annotations` module only matches suspend methods; Flow-returning methods are handled by the generic annotation instrumentation, while this project's Flow module supplies async completion and remains enabled separately. As written, this metadata incorrectly implies that the new default-off selector controls Flow support. Separate the two behaviors in the description.
